svg.text: BeliefLab | a small Bellman residual can hide a large value error
Constant reward 1/100, discount 99/100, zero-decision base value 0. Exact, prescribed fixture.
Signed bounds retain direction: reward -1/100 gives residual -1/100 and exact value -1.
A hidden-state example: bracket V* over every initial belief
Static state. Perfect probe costs 1/10. Discount 1/2. Base horizon 3; one extra backup.
b = probability of hidden state 0. Piecewise lines use exact rational breakpoints, not a belief grid.
Value bracket only: the finite tree is not an infinite-horizon policy. Discount 1 is refused.
Supplied-model guarantee, not learned-model validity, action optimality, policy-loss or real-world safety.
